messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert — streaming decode tail p99 elevated in prod across multiple regions. Metric decode_streaming_p99 increased from ~700ms to ~2.1s starting ~08:12 UTC. Affected: hosted inference (v1/v2) and several dedicated pools.

olivia: I'm on it, checking dashboards and recent deploys. Any kernel/driver changes in the last 3 hours?

samir: We had a TRT8 + flashattn driver rollout that started ~07:50 UTC — canary then progressive. I noted it earlier in deploy channel but canary looked OK at the time.

mike: Confirmed tag trt8-driver-2026-03-15 with compilepath-opt enabled.

tess: p95 also drifting — p95 streaming decode moved 180ms -> ~820ms during that window. Feels like paging/working-set growth.

rachel: CS reporting a few enterprise customers on Dedicated seeing session reconnects and poor streaming tails. Not full outage but SLO breaches.

olivia: Samir, can you pull the compilepath/driver diff from the rollout?

samir: Pulling now. Key changes: flashattn fusion turned on and kernel_alloc_window bumped from 16MB -> 32MB. Paste: ```diff
- flashattn_fusion = off
+ flashattn_fusion = on
- kernel_alloc_window = 16MB
+ kernel_alloc_window = 32MB
```

mike: That lines up with timing. Fusion yields bigger fused kernels -> larger transient memory. On streaming workloads with large KV caches this can trigger more GPU page evictions -> host roundtrips -> tail latency.

tess: I'm seeing NV_PAGE_FAULT counters spike on affected nodes in syslogs.

rachel: Logs show nv_pagefault_count spikes at 07:52, 07:56, 08:04 and two kernel OOMs in us-west-2 that recovered after eviction.

olivia: Mitigation options: 1) rollback driver/compilepath artifacts on clusters, 2) pin runtime routing to legacy kernel variant for hosted API (kernel-legacy), 3) temporarily scale Dedicated pools, 4) increase KV-cache eviction aggressiveness. What do we want to try first?

samir: Fastest/lowest-risk is to pin routing for hosted to `kernel-legacy-v1` via router flag. That avoids full rollback and buys time. I can flip it now.

mike: I'll open an emergency rollback PR for the compilepath changes and hold progressive rollout.

tess: I'll trigger emergency autoscale for Dedicated pools in impacted regions (+~20%) and enable burst capacity.

rachel: I'll prepare a short customer status update for CS.

olivia: Samir, use `routerctl set-route --model all --kernel kernel-legacy-v1 --duration 2h --reason 'emergency paging mitigation'` and confirm.

samir: Running `routerctl set-route --model all --kernel kernel-legacy-v1 --duration 2h --reason 'emergency paging mitigation'` now.

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Rolling routing change to edge/primary regions.

samir: Routing change in flight — edges reporting success in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, global in ~2m.

tess: Dedicated autoscale executed: +18% nodes us-west-2, +22% eu-west-1. Burst capacity enabled.

olivia: Monitoring dashboards — p99 started falling in canary region. us-west p99 dropped 2.1s -> 1.1s after routing switch.

mike: PR #4123 opened to revert flashattn_fusion and kernel_alloc_window to previous values. Marked emergency.

rachel: Drafting customer note: 'Investigating elevated streaming tail latency. Mitigations underway: routing pinned to legacy kernel; autoscaling enabled for Dedicated pools. No data loss. Update in 30m.' Approve to send?

olivia: Approve and send. Samir, coordinate rollback timing with Mike. Avoid full rollback until canary revert validated.

samir: Agreed. I'll keep routing pinned for 2h and monitor. After PR merge and artifact deployment to canary we'll watch memory and pgfault metrics.

mike: Revert artifacts queued; ETA for canary deploy ~25m after merge.

tess: Pushing a temporary compiler flag override on edge nodes to disable fusion: `COMPPATH_FLAGS=--no-flash-fusion` via config overlay. Rolling to canary now. Low-risk.

olivia: If p99 doesn't improve within 15m, escalate to full driver rollback and trigger customer SLA process.

samir: p99 trending down: us-west 1.1s -> 0.6s, eu-west 2.0s -> 0.8s.

deploy-bot: Canary revert deployment started: trt8-driver-2026-03-15-revert -> canary clusters.

rachel: Sent initial customer note to impacted enterprise contacts and CS channel.

tess: Increased KV-cache eviction rate on pinned clusters as extra mitigation — should cut page faults.

olivia: Action items recap: Samir (routing pin + monitor); Mike (PR + rollback pipeline); Tess (autoscale + eviction tuning); Rachel (customer comms). Update thread when complete.

samir: Acknowledged, staying on channel.

mike: PR merged, artifacts built. Canary revert healthy after ~12m. Memory footprint back to baseline and pagefaults down ~80% on canary.

samir: Progressive revert to broader regions starting now.

deploy-bot: Progressive rollout in progress: 6/24 clusters completed.

olivia: p99 improving as rollback progresses. Monitoring closely.

rachel: Customer update: 'We rolled back a compilepath optimization that increased memory pressure; mitigations applied and we are monitoring for stability. Postmortem to follow.'

tess: Autoscale will remain for ~1h to smooth traffic, then we'll scale down.

samir: Hand-off notes for next oncall: keep routing pinned until revert completes globally and p99 stable for 30m post-rollout. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-paging.

olivia: Filing incident ticket and assigning postmortem. Incident owner: olivia. Severity: Sev2 (SLO breach, partial customer impact).

rachel: Postmortem starter notes: root cause = compilepath flashattn fusion + increased kernel_alloc_window => working set blowup => increased GPU pagefaults => streaming tail latency. Contributing factors: progressive rollout without mem-footprint preflight and lack of load-profile gating.

olivia: Handing off to @samir and @mike for follow-up. :thumbsup:

samir: Taking follow-up until 17:00 UTC. Leaving channel but reachable.

olivia: last_message: Incident resolved for this shift: mitigations applied, rollback complete, p95/p99 within SLOs, customers notified. Closing thread in 1h if stable.
